content.text: Intent
MeetingSlotFinder

is a Java class that answers one question for a single day: what is the earliest time slot in which every attendee is free for a meeting of a given length? It takes each attendee's busy times, the working hours (for example 09:00–17:00) and the meeting length in minutes, and returns the earliest slot, or the result "no slot" when none fits. It serves anyone scheduling a meeting across several calendars, and gives the same answer every time for the same input.
Scope
IN: one day, any number of attendees, busy times as start–end pairs, working hours as one start–end pair, meeting length in minutes, result = earliest slot or "no slot".
OUT: multiple days, time zones, recurring meetings, rooms or other resources, ranking of alternative slots, reading real calendars, any screen or stored data.
Acceptance examples use working hours 09:00–17:00 unless stated.
Scenarios
None — a single computation with no ordered journey.
Requirements
R1: The system SHALL return the earliest slot of the requested length that lies inside no attendee's busy time.
R2: The system SHALL treat busy times of one attendee or of different attendees that overlap or touch (one ends exactly when the next starts) as one busy block.

R3: The system SHALL return only slots that lie entirely inside the working hours; a slot starting at or after the working-hours start and ending at or before the working-hours end is allowed, anything crossing either boundary is not. Busy time outside the working hours has no effect.
R4: The system SHALL start every slot on a 15-minute step (:00, :15, :30, :45).
R5: IF no slot of the requested length fits, THEN the system SHALL return "no slot" and never a shorter or partial slot.
R6: WHERE an attendee has no busy times, the system SHALL treat that attendee as free all day.
P1: The same input always gives the same result, regardless of the order of attendees or of the busy times within an attendee.

R7: IF the input is invalid — a missing (null) input, no attendees, a meeting length of zero or less, a busy time whose end is not after its start, or working hours whose end is not after their start — THEN the system SHALL reject it with an error and return no result.

R8: WHERE a meeting length or a busy time is not a multiple of 15 minutes, the system SHALL accept it and use the exact minutes given: the slot still starts on a 15-minute step (R4) and lasts exactly the meeting length, and a busy time blocks exactly the minutes it spans.
Data model
None — a pure computation; no stored nouns.
User interface
None — no user-facing surface; the class is called from code.
Dependencies
None — no other specs, entities or external systems.
Constraints
Considered, none apply: authorization, performance, volume, availability, audit, privacy, locale, cost. The class holds no state and has no side effects.
Acceptance criteria
A1 (verifies R1, R2): WHEN Ana is busy 09:00–10:00 and Sam is busy 09:30–11:00 and the meeting is 30 minutes, the system SHALL return 11:00–11:30.
A2 (verifies R2): WHEN Ana is busy 09:00–10:00 and 10:00–10:30 (touching) and Sam has no busy times, with a 30-minute meeting, the system SHALL return 10:30–11:00.
A3 (verifies R1): WHEN Ana is busy 09:00–10:00 and Sam is busy 10:30–17:00 and the meeting is 30 minutes, the system SHALL return 10:00–10:30 (a gap exactly as long as the meeting fits).
A4 (verifies R5): WHEN Ana is busy 09:00–10:00 and Sam is busy 10:15–17:00 and the meeting is 30 minutes, the system SHALL return "no slot" (the 15-minute gap is too short).
A5 (verifies R3, R5): WHEN Ana is busy 09:00–16:45 and the meeting is 30 minutes, the system SHALL return "no slot" (16:45–17:15 crosses the end of working hours).
A6 (verifies R3): WHEN Ana is busy 09:00–16:30 and the meeting is 30 minutes, the system SHALL return 16:30–17:00.

A7 (verifies R3): WHEN Ana is busy 08:00–09:30 and 17:00–18:00 and the meeting is 30 minutes, the system SHALL return 09:30–10:00, and WHEN Ana is busy only 07:00–08:00, the system SHALL return 09:00–09:30.
A8 (verifies R6): WHEN no attendee has busy times and the meeting is 60 minutes, the system SHALL return 09:00–10:00.
A9 (verifies R6, R1): WHEN Ana has no busy times and Sam is busy 09:00–12:00 and the meeting is 45 minutes, the system SHALL return 12:00–12:45.

A10 (verifies R5): WHEN the meeting is 480 minutes and Ana is busy 12:00–12:15, the system SHALL return "no slot", and WHEN the meeting is 480 minutes and nobody is busy, the system SHALL return 09:00–17:00.
A11 (verifies R2, R4): WHEN Ana is busy 09:00–09:15 and Sam is busy 09:15–09:30 and the meeting is 30 minutes, the system SHALL return 09:30–10:00.

A12 (verifies P1): WHEN the input of A1 is given with the attendees in the opposite order and with each attendee's busy times in reverse order, and when the same input is given twice, the system SHALL return 11:00–11:30 every time.

A13 (verifies R7): WHEN the meeting length is 0, or −15, or a busy time is 10:00–10:00 or 10:30–10:00, or working hours are 17:00–09:00, or the attendee list is empty, or any input is null, the system SHALL reject the call with an error and return no slot result.
A14 (verifies R8, R4): WHEN nobody is busy and the meeting is 20 minutes, the system SHALL return 09:00–09:20.

A15 (verifies R8, R4): WHEN Ana is busy 09:10–09:40 and the meeting is 30 minutes, the system SHALL return 09:45–10:15 (09:40 is not a 15-minute step, so the next step is used), and WHEN Ana is busy 09:00–09:10, the system SHALL return 09:15–09:45.
Migration & compatibility
None — new class, nothing exists to migrate.
Artifacts
None.
Open Questions
None — the author decided invalid input is rejected with an error (R7) and off-step lengths and busy times are accepted with exact minutes (R8).
